implementations.name: RecipeDeleteDialog
implementations.moduleDoc:
@commise/features-recipes — web recipe delete-confirmation dialog (T068 building block; spec §6.5).

The recipe's delete confirmation, as the design system's `ConfirmDialog`: it names the recipe, offers "Delete recipe"
(the filled destructive tone, `trash`) and "Keep recipe" (where focus opens), spins the confirm while `deleting`, says
"Deleting…" politely, and shows a failure inside the dialog (B17). It performs NO mutation — the composing app wires
the delete to `onConfirm` — and every close path (Escape, the Keep button) is the one `onCancel`.

Focus returns to the sibling control that opened it on close (`ConfirmDialog`'s `useReturnFocusOnClose`).

Presentational: props → JSX, with no data, no mutation and no effect of its own.

implementations.name: RecipeMakePublicDialog
implementations.moduleDoc:
@commise/features-recipes — "Make this recipe public?", the confirm a downgraded owner sees before a private
recipe goes public (UX SPECIFY 2026-10-15; plan 2026-10-14-009 Q5). One component for both platforms: the design
system's `ConfirmDialog` resolves to its Radix leaf on web and its `DialogFrame` leaf on native.

Making a private recipe public is destructive in the design system's sense — anyone may save a copy of a public
recipe — so the primitive is used as it is (public is NOT final, owner ruling 2026-10-26, and the body never says it
is): the danger-filled
"Make public" against "Keep private", where focus opens. The body says the cost plainly, per reason
(`makePublicConsequence`). ⛔ Nothing here sells: no Premium button and no third choice (DSA Art. 25; the
deceptive-pattern rule) — under `upsell` the body states the fact and the ⋯ menu's Make private is where Premium is.

Presentational: props → JSX, no data, no mutation, no effect of its own.

implementations.name: RecipeCard
implementations.moduleDoc:
@commise/features-recipes/card — the web recipe card: one data shape, three variants
(`docs/design/uiOverhaul/buildSpec.md` §4.1).

- **grid** — a 4:3 cover with its chips, then the title, the meta line (time · difficulty · rating · calories) and
  the timestamp. It is a SUBGRID four rows tall, so in a library or Home grid every card's rows line up with its
  neighbours' and an empty row keeps its track.
- **row** — the list view: an 80 × 80 cover, the title on up to two lines, the same meta line and a status line.

No variant shows servings, cuisine, the tags, the version, a cover time chip or a difficulty badge (designer ruling
2026-11-02, `docs/design/uiRefreshWorkshop5/nativeBoards/designAnswers.md`); difficulty is a plain word in the meta line.
- **compact** — Home below a 960 container: the cover with its chips, then the title.

The variant is decided by `cardVariantOf` in the orchestration layer and handed in; selecting an arrangement of one
data shape is display derivation, which a render component may do (§11.1). A custom arrangement of the
`RecipeCard.*` parts (`children`) still works for the surfaces that compose their own.

The whole card is ONE link (or, with no `href`, one button) named by the title, stretched over the card by a
pseudo-element, so nothing is nested inside it. The surface is a level-1 card — `paper`, a `lineDivider` hairline,
`shadow-sm`, `shadow-md` on hover with a fine pointer — and never glass (owner ruling D12). Every colour is a role, so
the card follows the browser's scheme (D15).

The rules the parts draw are decided in `./recipeCardView.ts`, shared with the native leaf: an absent difficulty
renders nothing; PRO follows the materialized flag; a draft's status replaces its visibility;
an unrated recipe says so.

props.name: children
props.description: The arrangement.

props.name: fullMeta
props.description:
The compact tile only: draw the list row's whole meta line (time · difficulty · rating · calories). Without it the
compact tile draws the brief line, the time then the calories (Home's tile; designer, 2026-11-03). The Recipes grid
asks, because its tile is the compact variant in size and a list row's equal in what it says. The grid and the
row always draw the whole line and ignore it.

props.name: headingLevel
props.description:
The heading level of the title on the WEB leaf (`buildSpec.md` §4.1 "Card title is H3 on a sectioned page"). The
surface knows where the card sits in the page's outline and the card does not: a results list straight under the
page's H1 passes `2`, a card under a section's H2 (Home's Recent recipes, a Discover rail) passes `3`. Required,
so no card guesses; the native leaf has no heading outline and does not read it.

props.name: href
props.description:
Where the card leads, which makes it a real link on web (open in a new tab, copy the address). Native has no URLs
and ignores it, the same web-only convention the list's source switcher follows.

props.name: nutrition
props.description:
The recipe's per-serving nutrition, as an already-decided NODE rendered in the meta line.

A SLOT rather than a field, because the figure is a DEFERRED lookup that lands after the card does:
the list holds the lookup and decides what belongs here (a `RecipeNutritionSlot` over the page's batch
reading, or nothing at all), and the card stays pure and knows nothing about loading. An
ABSENT slot renders no item at all — the same absent-value rule as difficulty, cuisine and tags, and
never a placeholder or a fabricated 0.

⚠️ It is `RecipeCard.Meta` (and the row's meta line) that renders this. A custom arrangement (`children`) that
omits `.Meta` DROPS the slot silently — unlike a misplaced part, which throws — because an unrendered optional
node is indistinguishable from an absent one. `RecipeDiscoveryCard` and `CollectionMemberRow` are exactly such
arrangements, so check for `<RecipeCard.Meta />` before concluding the figure never arrived.

props.name: onSelect
props.description:
When provided, the card is actionable and reports the recipe id. On web with an `href`, a plain click is handed
here and a modified click (new tab) follows the link.

props.name: showEdited
props.description:
The compact tile only: draw the version and timestamp line ("Edited 2d ago") under the title, as the grid does. Home's
tile does not ask, so it stays the cover and the title; the Recipes list asks, because a Recipes sort may not be by
recency (designer, 2026-11-02). A surface `footer` replaces it, as in the grid; the grid and the row ignore it.

props.name: variant
props.description: The variant the orchestration decided with `cardVariantOf`.

implementations.name: RecipeCard
implementations.moduleDoc:
@commise/features-recipes/card — the native recipe card: one data shape, three variants
(`docs/design/uiOverhaul/buildSpec.md` §4.1), the twin of the web leaf.

- **grid** — a 4:3 cover with its chips, then the title, the meta line (time · difficulty · rating · calories) and
  the timestamp.
- **row** — the list view: an 80 × 80 cover, the title on up to two lines, the same meta line and a status line.
- **compact** — the cover with its chips, then the title and a brief meta line (time, calories); the whole line with `fullMeta`.

The orchestration layer decides the variant with `cardVariantOf`; this leaf draws the arrangement it is handed. The
card is ONE pressable link named by the title. Its surface is a level-1 card — `paper`, a `lineDivider` hairline,
the `sm` elevation — and never glass (owner ruling D12). Every colour is read from `useTheme()` at render, so the
card follows the system scheme (D15); the stylesheet holds layout only.

iOS masks a layer's shadow when the same layer clips, so the elevation sits on an outer shell that never clips and the
clip on the content view inside it.

The meta line wraps and never clips: native has no `:empty`, so it spaces its items with a gap rather than the web's
middots — a nutrition slot that settles on nothing would otherwise leave an orphan separator. A part that does not fit
moves to the next line. A badge line is a wrapping row of EXACTLY one line's height (`./oneLine.ts`, scaled by the OS
font scale), so an item that does not fit wraps to a second line that is fully hidden (W-06).

No variant shows servings, cuisine, the tags, the version, a cover time chip or a difficulty badge (designer ruling
2026-11-02, `docs/design/uiRefreshWorkshop5/nativeBoards/designAnswers.md`); difficulty is a plain word in the meta line.

components.name: RecipeCardGridSkeleton
patterns: Null Object — the loading phase's stand-in for the cards

implementations.name: RecipeCardGridSkeleton
implementations.moduleDoc:
@commise/features-recipes — the ONE authoritative web recipe-card loading skeleton.

**Pattern: Null Object for the loading phase.** A single presentational unit (pure `props → JSX`) that stands in for
the recipe cards while the first page is in flight. Every web surface that paints recipe cards composes THIS
component, so "what a loading recipe card looks like" has exactly one representation.

Three invariants it exists to hold:

 1. **The live region carries its label as CONTENT, not only as `aria-label`.** An empty `role="status"` is
    zero-height and silent, because a live region announces its content, not its label.
 2. **It draws the variant the loaded cards will use, in their grid** (`docs/design/uiOverhaul/buildSpec.md` §4.1:
    "the same rows at the same sizes"), from the same class strings as the populated grid (`./cardGridClass.ts`), so
    nothing moves when the page lands.
 3. **It pulses once, for one second, in `surfaceMuted`**, and not at all under reduced motion. The placeholders are
    decorative (`aria-hidden`); the caption alone announces the wait.

`RecipeCardGridSkeleton.native.tsx` is its RN counterpart.

implementations.name: CollectionDetailBody
implementations.moduleDoc:
@commise/features-recipes/collections — the SETTLED collection detail, composed once for web and mobile
(`docs/design/uiOverhaul/buildSpec.md` §5.2, §5.3): the {@link CollectionHeader} (back, name, meta, description, Add
recipes and the ⋯ menu), the two failure lines, the {@link CollectionMembers} list, and the sheets the header opens —
rename, delete, make-public, Premium, the add-recipes picker and the pull-updates dialog.

The header and the parts after it each take their own side gutter on native (`CollectionDetailGutter`): the screen's
scroller does not pad, because the large title insets itself.

Orchestration: every piece it draws is a leaf pair that resolves per platform, and what it reads is the
{@link CollectionDetail} view-model — plain `.tsx` with no native twin. The app keeps only what differs: the frame around it (a page `<section>` on
web, a `ScrollView` on mobile), the read boundary, the navigation, and the links web needs so a card is a real anchor.

The picker's read boundary is the app's (`ClientQueryBoundary` on web, `QueryBoundary` on mobile; this package may
not import `@commise/query`), handed in as {@link CollectionDetailBodyProps.PickerBoundary}.

implementations.moduleDoc:
@commise/features-recipes — web collection-list FRAME (presentational).

The chrome of the collection list — the heading and the create action — rendered OUTSIDE the list's suspense
boundary, which the composing container passes as `children`. A pending or failed read therefore swaps only what is
under the header, never the header itself. It fetches nothing.

The heading takes focus when `headingFocusSignal` advances: a retry from the refresh notice (inside the boundary)
that succeeds removes the button the viewer pressed, and the container reports that across the boundary.

@commise/features-recipes — native collection-list FRAME (presentational).

The React Native leaf of `CollectionListFrame`: the large title (slice 3) and the floating "New collection", around
whatever the list's suspense boundary renders as `children`, so a pending or failed read never unmounts them. It
fetches nothing.

The large title and the segments are not drawn here: the frame hands them to the one list below it through
`RecipeListHeaderContext` (the same slot the Recipes frame uses), and the list draws them as its first child, so they
scroll away with the content (designer finding C-2) and never unmount when the read changes state. The search field is the
one thing that stays (designer ruling 2026-11-02): where the list has one it is drawn ONCE here, over a spacer the header
holds, slides with the scroll and pins at the top on a band, through `@commise/ui/pinned-search`, the same parts the Recipes
frame uses.

When `headingFocusSignal` advances — a retry from the refresh notice inside the boundary succeeded and removed the
button the viewer pressed — the screen-reader cursor moves to the heading.

what renders inside the list's suspense boundary once the read has settled.

The search from six collections and the count, the refresh notice, then the first run — whose action depends on
whether the cook has recipes to group yet — a no-match for the search, or the album cards in a two-column grid that
becomes `auto-fill` from a 600 container, then the server-paged "Load more". Pure: the container reads and narrows.

list reads, and no member photos are embedded), so the card is the collection's tint and monogram with its name,
visibility and copy credit. A recipe-service contract change is owed for the rest.

implementations.name: CollectionLoadError
implementations.moduleDoc:
@commise/features-recipes/collections — `CollectionLoadError`: what a collection read's boundary renders when
the read fails. A 404 is final (the collection was deleted, or is not the viewer's), so it says why and offers no retry;
any other failure is the generic one, whose retry is the boundary's reset, which refetches. The host names the way back, because only it knows
where back goes, and passes it only for a missing collection.

ONE file for both apps: the design system's `StateNotice` is a platform pair, so the web page gets an alert in its flow
and the mobile screen gets the thumb-reach stack. It replaces the web app's raw-`<button>` copy and the mobile screen's
hand-built fallback.

before a private collection goes public (plan 2026-10-14-009 T1). The collection twin of `RecipeMakePublicDialog`:

implementations.name: PullUpdatesDialog
implementations.moduleDoc:
@commise/features-recipes — web Pull-Updates preview dialog (W5 Task 10, C2 / FR-011).

Presentational (pure props → JSX) render of the collection-view wireframe's "Pull Updates Preview
Dialog". Built on the house **Radix `Dialog`** (mirrors `PhotoCarousel`'s lightbox usage, B6/CR-003):
Radix owns the focus trap, Escape-to-dismiss, and background inert, so this component hand-rolls none of
that (no `role="dialog"` div). `open` is driven entirely by the caller — `onOpenChange` maps Radix's own
close paths (Escape, backdrop click) onto the same `onCancel` the explicit Cancel control uses, so there
is exactly ONE exit path, not two.

Focus-return is handled explicitly, NOT left to Radix's default: `Dialog.Content`'s built-in
`onCloseAutoFocus` only restores focus to an OWNED `Dialog.Trigger` (`DialogContentModal` unconditionally
`preventDefault()`s FocusScope's own restore-to-previous-element behavior and focuses
`context.triggerRef.current` instead — see `@radix-ui/react-dialog`'s `DialogContentModal`). This dialog
is opened by a sibling control (the collection-actions "Pull Updates" button, wired in W5 Task 12), not
an owned `Dialog.Trigger`, so that default silently focuses nothing. `useReturnFocusOnClose`
(`@commise/ui/dialog-focus`) owns the repair for every surface in this position: it snapshots
`document.activeElement` at the render where `open` flips true — BEFORE `Dialog.Content` (and its
autofocus-on-mount) ever commits — and returns the `onCloseAutoFocus` handler that restores it,
`preventDefault()`ing Radix's own no-op default so there is one focus-restore path, not a silently-losing
second one. Its module doc carries the rest, including why the edge latch must not be a ref.

The Cancel and Pull actions sit in the design-system `DialogActions`, which stacks them full width on a phone, Pull on
top, so the pair cannot overflow a 320 px dialog.

A discriminated three-way state (mutually exclusive, matching {@link PullUpdatesDialogProps}'s JSDoc):
(1) a `role="status"` progress affordance while `isLoadingPreview`, or before any `diff` has arrived; (2)
a `role="alert"` for a failed preview/commit — `'drift'` (409, the previewed diff went stale) is
deliberately NOT a dead end: the counts are hidden (they're no longer trustworthy) but Cancel/Escape
still close the dialog, so the composing container (W5 Task 12) can re-run the preview; (3) the loaded
`diff` — added/removed/unchanged COUNTS only (this block never resolves recipe titles, it only received
ids), the "not overwritten" note, and the count-templated Pull action, disabled while `isCommitting` or
when there is nothing to add.

The React Native leaf of `PullUpdatesDialog`: a
{@link FullScreenSheet} rendering the SAME controlled, presentational contract as the web leaf — same
state precedence, same localized copy, so the two platforms can't drift. `onRequestClose` (the Android
hardware-back / web-Escape path RN provides) is wired straight to `onCancel`, the same callback the
explicit Cancel control uses — one exit path, not two, mirroring the web leaf's `onOpenChange`→`onCancel`
wiring.

The modal window and its safe-area padding belong to `FullScreenSheet`, not here. This leaf previously
hand-rolled `<Modal presentationStyle="fullScreen">` over a flat `padding: 20` surface, which on an
edge-to-edge Android device drew the heading UNDER the status bar — fully occluded, and therefore absent
from the accessibility hierarchy, which is how Maestro's `collectionsPull` flow caught it — and put the
Cancel/Pull row UNDER the navigation bar's own tap targets.

The Cancel and Pull actions sit in the design-system `DialogActions`, which stacks them full width on a phone, Pull on
top, instead of a row that clips the first button.

A discriminated three-way state (mutually exclusive, matching {@link PullUpdatesDialogProps}'s JSDoc):
(1) a `progressbar` affordance while `isLoadingPreview`, or before any `diff` has arrived; (2) an `alert`
for a failed preview/commit — `'drift'` (409, the previewed diff went stale) is deliberately NOT a dead
end: the counts are hidden (they're no longer trustworthy) but Cancel/back still close the dialog, so the
composing container (W5 Task 12) can re-run the preview; (3) the loaded `diff` — added/removed/unchanged
COUNTS only (this block never resolves recipe titles, it only received ids), the "not overwritten" note,
and the count-templated Pull action, busy while `isCommitting`, disabled when there is nothing to add.

@commise/features-recipes/dataSources — web Data sources PAGE frame (presentational; plan R55, design §S16).

The page's heading and its two intro sentences, rendered OUTSIDE the read's boundary, which the composing route
passes as `children`. So a loading, failed or offline read swaps only what is under the intro, and the page never
loses its title. One column, the `reading` width, at every width; Back goes to Profile (`buildSpec.md` §9.2). The heading takes focus when
`headingFocusSignal` advances: a retry that took Try again away.

With a way back the page sits in the design system's `PushedPageFrame`, so Back is pinned in a bar below 840 and the
header's own eyebrow carries it from 840 (`docs/design/uiRefreshWorkshop5/pinnedBackBar.md` §6). Without one there is
nowhere to go back to, so there is no bar and no frame.

implementations.name: AmbiguityReview
implementations.moduleDoc:
The U13 AMBIGUITY REVIEW surface (web) — D7/R9's author affordance on recipe detail — and the one-time CLONE banner.

ENTRY is the count notice + a disclosure toggle; DISMISSAL (closing it) is always safe, because each pick is its own
write. One row per AMBIGUOUS LINE ({@link ambiguityReviewLines}), and a pick re-points THAT line alone, through the
rebind command, as the editor's row 7 does for a stored line (`useAmbiguityPick`). Each row's shortlist, sentences and
pick are `useAmbiguityReviewRow`'s. The row's status line sits after its chips and speaks once, at the end of the
answer.

A taken pick's line is no longer ambiguous, so its row leaves the review. The surface then says the pick saved, in a
status line that takes focus from the row that went (WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.3) and stays after the last row has gone.

Only the OWNER is offered picks: the rebind is owner-checked, so anyone else's pick could only fail. The clone banner
is not a review and has no pick; it shows to whoever the clone response reached.

ORCHESTRATION: the exported component selects the owner's review or the banner alone, by `viewerIsOwner`. The
owner's review holds the pick command, and each row its own state (`useAmbiguityReviewRow`).

DESIGN PATTERN: platform leaf over shared pure models (`ambiguityReviewLines`, `ambiguousNotice`,
`clonePrivateFoodsBannerText`), the shared pick controller and the shared row hook — the `RecipeDetailBody` /
`needsReviewSurface` composition, extended.

implementations.name: PhotoCarousel
implementations.moduleDoc:
@commise/features-recipes — web recipe-photo carousel + lightbox (W2 Task 2.2, D2). It is the recipe
detail's hero (`RecipeHero`), so it is the screen's one photo surface (F2).

Replaces the static photo grid with a swipeable, scroll-snap strip of slides, a dot-navigation strip
(shown only when there is more than one photo), and a full-screen lightbox opened by activating a slide.

Pattern: the lightbox is the house **Radix `Dialog`** (per B6) — Radix owns the focus trap, Escape-to-
dismiss, background inert, and focus-return to the activating slide, so this component hand-rolls none of
that (`aria-modal` div). The open slide is ephemeral, self-contained view state (`activeIndex`), not data
or a behavior-switching prop, so it stays local to this interactive widget rather than lifting to the
orchestration container (nothing else consumes it — YAGNI).

HERO PAGING (`nativeBoards/buildLists.md` item 1): paging chevrons at the sides and dots that track the page. The page is
state, read from the strip's scroll offset and set directly when a chevron is pressed; a chevron scrolls the next
slide into view (`block: 'nearest'`, so the page itself does not move). The slide pitch is read from the slides, not
assumed, so the strip's gap can change without breaking the rule.

B7: offscreen slides are `loading="lazy"` so a 10-photo recipe does not eagerly paint ~50 MB of
full-size originals; the lightbox image is eager (the user asked to see it). A service-side gallery
thumbnail rendition remains the fuller fix (tracked with the gallery projection) — out of scope here.

implementations.name: PhotoCarousel
implementations.moduleDoc:
@commise/features-recipes — native recipe-photo carousel + lightbox (W2 Task 2.2, D2).

The React Native leaf of `PhotoCarousel`: a horizontal, paging
`ScrollView` of photo slides, a dot-indicator row (only when there is more than one photo), and a
full-screen `Modal` lightbox opened by tapping a slide. Same read model, same accessible names, and the
same branch behaviour as the web leaf so the two platforms can't drift.

A `ScrollView` (not a `FlatList`) backs the strip: a recipe has at most `MAX_PHOTOS_PER_RECIPE` (≤10)
photos, so `FlatList` virtualization buys nothing here while complicating layout/testing — the simplest
correct paging container wins (KISS/YAGNI). The open slide is ephemeral local view state, not data.

⛔ A SLIDE IS THE STRIP'S WIDTH, FROM THE STRIP'S OWN LAYOUT (`docs/design/compactHeightLayout.md` §8). It used to be
the window's width inside a strip 32 dp and the side insets narrower, so `pagingEnabled` (which pages by the strip's
width) drifted by that much per slide, upright as well as sideways. The slides render once the container reports its
width; the strip sits below the fold, so the one-frame wait does not show. The box is `carouselBox`: 4:3 at that
width, capped at 40% of the window's height, and narrowed to keep 4:3, so a sideways phone shows a photo rather than
a slide taller than the screen. The strip is exactly one slide wide and centred.

The lightbox is drawn edge to edge, and its photo and its 48 dp Close sit inside the safe area, so a side navigation
bar or a cutout never covers either.

HERO PAGING (`nativeBoards/buildLists.md` item 1): paging chevrons at the sides and dots that track the page. The page
is state: read from the strip's scroll offset and set directly when a chevron is pressed.

§6, the first slice of 008 FR-035).

The PURE render half of the recipe page, in reading order: the hero, the back link, the rating card, the cuisine eyebrow
and the title, the status row, the source line and byline, the fact tiles, the actions, the Screen on row, the
description and the tags; then the body — one column below a 720 px body, and from 720 two columns, ingredients (5/12,
sticky with its own scroll) beside the steps (7/12), with the review surface under the steps. The collapsed Nutrition
row sits before the columns, full width.

There is no section switch (`nativeBoards/buildLists.md`): the page is one scroll. Left out until their features
ship (`designAnswers.md` section "2026-11-02: card, Home header and Recipe detail build questions", bullets
"8 comments" row and "Start cooking"): the comments row and "Start cooking".

Every width rule is a CONTAINER query on the article (`@container/detail`), never a script measurement, so the
server render and the hydrated page are the same page. "Screen on" is a labelled row, and the toggle itself renders
nothing where the browser cannot keep the screen awake.

Its orchestration shell — `RecipeDetailView.tsx`, which binds the serving scale, the cook's marks, Screen on and
the description's disclosure — is a separate file because a file does ONE thing (CODING_STANDARDS §1).

implementations.name: RecipeDetailBody
implementations.moduleDoc:
@commise/features-recipes — native recipe-detail view (T066 building block; `nativeBoards/buildLists.md`, the
`RecipeDetailAndroid384` board).

The React Native leaf of the recipe page, in reading order: the hero; the rating card; the cuisine eyebrow and the
title; the status row; the source line and byline; the fact tiles; the actions; the Screen on row; the description
and the tags; then the ingredients (serves in the heading, tap-to-check rows), the steps (the current step), the
nutrition, the review surface. From a 720 pt body the ingredients and the steps sit side by side.

It renders the page's ONE scroller. Every section is a direct child of the scroll content, one flat list. There is no
section switch: the page is one scroll, and "Screen on" is a labelled row in the page, drawn once.

Left out until their features ship (`designAnswers.md` section
"2026-11-02: card, Home header and Recipe detail build questions", bullets "8 comments" row and "Start cooking"):
the comments row and "Start cooking".

This is the PURE render half. Its orchestration shell, `RecipeDetailView.native.tsx`, binds the session state and
measures the layout, because a file does ONE thing (CODING_STANDARDS §1).

implementations.name: RecipeDetailView
implementations.moduleDoc:
@commise/features-recipes — web recipe-detail view (T066 building block).

The ORCHESTRATION SHELL of the recipe page, and nothing else: it binds what the page holds for the cook — the
session serving scale, the cook's marks (`useCookMarks`, blueprint A13), the one "Screen on" state with its wake
lock (A20), and the description's and the Nutrition row's disclosures — and hands the pure render (`RecipeDetailBody.tsx`) the result. The
public contract (`RecipeDetailViewProps`) carries none of them, which is the point: an app composes this and cannot
ship the page with the scale, the checks or Screen on un-wired, because there is nothing for it to wire.

Screen on defaults to off on each visit and is released when the cook leaves the page (the hold's effect cleanup).

implementations.name: RecipeHero
implementations.moduleDoc: @commise/features-recipes — web recipe-detail HERO (mockup `screenRecipeDetail`). The recipe detail opens with its photos. The hero IS the photo carousel: slide 1 is the cover, because the service makes the cover `photos[0]` on every read path. It used to paint the cover as a separate image and then a second carousel below repeated it as slide 1 (F2, `docs/design/uiOverhaul/evaluateRecipeAndWizard.md`), so there is now one photo surface, built from `photos` alone (`specRecipeAndWizard.md` S2.1). ## No photo: the gradient band A recipe with no photo shows a 96 px band (`buildSpec.md` §1.8, §6.7) of the ONE no-photo gradient the cards use (sky to cream at 170 degrees), alone: no disc, no monogram and no cuisine on it (`designAnswers.md` 2026-11-02). It is drawn here until `RecipeCover` on fix/im-recipescard lands, which draws the same gradient at `aspect="band"`; the hero then renders that. It renders no `` (an empty `src` paints a broken-image glyph), keeps a real height, and is decorative, because the H1 names the recipe. The picture glyph in a 4:3 box it replaces read as "the image failed" (`evaluateFinal.md` F10). The leaf itself holds no state, fetches nothing and navigates nowhere; the carousel's open slide is the carousel's own view state. The mockup's overlaid back/share/save controls are NOT part of this leaf — those are navigation and mutations, so they belong to the orchestration layer.

implementations.name: RecipeLoadError
implementations.moduleDoc:
@commise/features-recipes/detail — `RecipeLoadError`: what a recipe read's boundary renders when the read fails.
A 404 is final, so it offers no retry; any other failure — including an id that cannot name a recipe, where there is no
evidence the recipe is gone — is the generic one, whose retry is the boundary's reset, which refetches. Both keep a way
back, which the host names ("Back to My recipes", "Back to Discover") because only it knows where back goes.

ONE file for both apps: the design system's `StateNotice` is a platform pair, so the web page gets an alert in its flow
and the mobile screen gets the thumb-reach stack.

components.name: RecipeSourceLine
patterns: Adapter — `onOpen` wraps the platform's URL opener

implementations.name: RecipeSourceLine
implementations.moduleDoc:
@commise/features-recipes — WEB recipe-source (provenance) line.

Pattern: **pure presentational (render) component** — `props → JSX`, one responsibility (say where this
recipe came from), no state, no fetching, no ref, and on this platform no side effect at all: the browser's
own `<a href>` IS the link adapter, so nothing is injected.

It renders for EVERY viewer. Provenance is a property of the recipe, not of who is looking — which is the
defect this component exists to close: attribution used to reach the screen only through
the old clone action, mounted only for a viewer who could clone, so the OWNER of an imported recipe could
never see where it came from and `sourceUrl` reached nobody.

SAFETY: `sourceUrl` is untrusted (an import pipeline wrote it, and the wire's `z.string().url()` happily
admits `javascript:`/`data:` — see `safeHttpUrl`). Two rules follow, and both are load-bearing:
 1. A URL becomes a link ONLY if `safeHttpUrl` admits it; a rejected URL is dropped entirely and never
    shown as raw text either.
 2. The LINK's visible text is the verified HOST, never `sourceAttribution`. Attribution is untrusted free
    text: a recipe claiming "Serious Eats" while pointing at `evil.example` must not be able to borrow
    that name as the label of the thing you click. Attribution renders beside the link, as text.

moduleTags.text: @commise/features-recipes — WEB recipe-source (provenance) line.

props.name: sourceAttribution
props.description: The author-stated provenance ("Serious Eats", "Grandma's cookbook").

props.name: sourceUrl
props.description: The recipe's original URL, as stored. Untrusted — gated by `safeHttpUrl` before it is ever linked.

implementations.name: RecipeSourceLine
implementations.moduleDoc:
@commise/features-recipes — NATIVE recipe-source (provenance) line: "Adapted from" and where.

The React Native leaf of `RecipeSourceLine`: same contract, same rules, same states. Renders for EVERY viewer,
because provenance belongs to the recipe, not to who is looking.

React Native has no declarative link, so opening a URL is a platform call, injected as `onOpen` and defaulting to
`openExternalUrl`.

SAFETY, sharper here than on web because this platform hands the string to the OS: `Linking.openURL` dispatches
`tel:`, `sms:` and `intent:` too, so a URL that `safeHttpUrl` refuses gets no tap target at all. The link text is the
VERIFIED HOST, never the untrusted `sourceAttribution`, which renders beside it as plain text.

implementations.name: ServingScaleControl
implementations.moduleDoc:
@commise/features-recipes — the serving-count control, ONE file for web and native (the Stepper resolves its own
platform leaf): the design system's `Stepper` bound to the recipe's
serving range (`buildSpec.md` §1.11, §6.1). It used to be a hand-built twin with a display-face (Manrope) number field; Manrope
never sets a number, and the control was built twice (F8, `evaluateFinal.md`).

The range IS `servingsRange(baseServings)` from the domain, so an option can never exist that the scaling policy
would reject — including for a recipe authored ABOVE the display cap, which must still sit at, and scale down from,
its own yield. Every value leaving here has been through `clampServings`.

Accessibility is the Stepper's: a group named "Servings" (its label hidden, because the heading row already says
"for {n}"), two named buttons that are `aria-disabled` with the press refused at the ends (never natively `disabled`,
which would drop focus, SC 2.4.3), and a polite announcement after a step — empty on open — that names the limit at
the ends, through `servingsAnnouncement`.

implementations.moduleDoc:
@commise/features-recipes — the web step row (build spec §6.1, §6.3).

The step text stays plain content: a whole-step button would make it presentational and hide it from a screen
reader (Settled 33). Its numeral is its own 44 px toggle, a `button` with `aria-pressed` named "Mark step {n} as
current"; the toggle's `::after` stretches over the whole step, so a tap anywhere on it moves the marker for pointer
users, and the timer chip sits above that overlay. The current step shows the 3 px `hereBar` at its start edge and
fills its numeral with `action`.

implementations.name: StepRow
implementations.moduleDoc:
@commise/features-recipes — the native step row (build spec §6.1, §6.3): the mirror of `StepRow.tsx`.

The step text stays content; the numeral is its own 44 pt `button` with a selected state, named "Mark step {n} as
current". A press anywhere else on the step activates the same toggle for touch users through an outer pressable
that is NOT an accessibility element, so a screen reader meets the text and the one button rather than a button
that swallows the text. The current step shows the 3 pt `hereBar` and fills its numeral with `action`.

The instruction and the timer are set by the design-system `Text` (ADR-0080), which turns system scaling off and draws
the size and leading itself. This is the migration only: it did NOT change the iOS clip of step 11 (QA batch 4, device
check at 08ae6ba75), whose cause is still open.

Presentational: props → JSX.

implementations.name: VariantDetailsDialog
implementations.moduleDoc:
details/VariantDetailsDialog — the details dialog, web (curated U14; `docs/design/ingredientSpecialization.md`
§S8.2 to §S8.8, §S9).

A presentational leaf: it renders the state `useVariantDetailsDialog` derived, which the host passes in, on the
design-system `Sheet`. The short list is a
single-select listbox whose selection does not follow focus; the long list is a search combobox that controls an
always-open listbox through `aria-activedescendant`, with each group a real `role="group"`.

Focus on load (§S8.6): the first row, the current row, the search input, or Try again. It moves only when focus is
still where the dialog put it, so a list that arrives late never pulls focus from a control the person chose.

implementations.name: DiscoveryBrowseRails
implementations.moduleDoc:
@commise/features-recipes/discovery/DiscoveryBrowseRails — (orchestration) the curated rails, each behind its OWN read boundary,
so one rail loads and fails without the others. Mounted only while browsing (or under a no-result state, for the one
rail), so the rail reads are a browse-time cost. A failed refresh of the rails on screen keeps their rows and is
reported once, for the block, through `useBrowseRailsRefresh`'s passive observers.

Pull-to-refresh and the scroll bind are handed to the rails leaf unconditionally: the native leaf uses them, the web
leaf ignores them (its contract), so this part has no platform branch.

implementations.name: DiscoveryFooter
implementations.moduleDoc:
@commise/features-recipes/discovery — the web footer of a Discover card (`docs/design/uiOverhaul/buildSpec.md`
§4.1): a 20 px avatar disc, "@handle" on one line (or "From {source}" for an imported recipe with no author), and a
44 px Save a copy icon button at the end.

The button's state is the copy's (`useSaveCopy`): the glyph fills while a copy is being made and stays filled once it
exists, a press while saving or saved sends nothing, and a failure unfills it and says so in an inline alert under the
row. It is `aria-disabled` rather than `disabled` while saving or saved, so it stays in the tab order and a keyboard
cook who just pressed it does not lose their place.

Presentational: it holds no state and sends nothing; the card lifts it above its link (`RecipeCard`'s `footer` slot).

implementations.name: DiscoveryHeaderGroup
implementations.moduleDoc:
@commise/features-recipes — the native discovery header group: the heading and the keyword field.

ONE group in every layout, the field its LAST child, so the field never changes parent or index and a remount never
costs it focus and its keyboard. Stacked, the large title sits over the field; in compact height (a phone held
sideways) the plain heading shares a wrapping row with it, so the results keep their room.

Presentational: props → JSX. The one effect it owns is the screen-reader cursor on the compact heading, which takes it
when `headingFocusSignal` advances.

`compact` selects the heading's presentation INSIDE this one group rather than choosing between two components in the
frame: two component types would remount the field on a rotation, and a remounted field loses its focus and keyboard.
`drawsHeading` is false when the filter panel is shown: the frame then draws the title once above the panel row, and
this group holds the field alone, still at the same index under the same parent, unpadded because that row pads.

implementations.name: DiscoveryResultsView
implementations.moduleDoc:
@commise/features-recipes/discovery/DiscoveryResultsView — (orchestration) the results of one search, from its pages: the rails
or the cards, the no-result state, and one nutrition batch per fetched page. Shared by the settled read and by the
"previous results" kept under a failed search.

The deferred calorie lookup (ADR-0079) is ONE REQUEST PER FETCHED PAGE: "Load more" appends, so a single batch over every
accumulated id would change its key on every page and drop the figures already on screen to skeletons. While the rails
are the body these cards are not on screen, so nothing is asked about them; and the compact card draws no figure, so a
batch for it would have nobody to read the promise (a rejection would go unhandled). The id list is unmemoized on
purpose: the lookup keys its batches on the ids' content, never on the array's identity.

implementations.name: DiscoveryScreen
implementations.moduleDoc:
@commise/features-recipes/discovery/DiscoveryScreen — public-recipe discovery (orchestration): the discovery
FRAME around a suspense read of the search, with the curated rails as the body while the viewer is browsing
(`docs/design/uiOverhaul/buildSpec.md` §4.4–§4.6). The web route and the mobile tab both render THIS; each supplies only
the {@link DiscoveryCriteriaStore} (URL / component state) and the {@link DiscoveryPlatform} (boundary, calorie lookup,
recent-search persistence), plus its own navigation.

The frame (heading, search field, filters, back-to-browse, sort, the count line) sits outside the read boundary, so a
pending or failed search swaps only the results. The boundary's loading body is `RecipeDiscoveryLoading` in the card
variant the results will draw, its error body is `RecipeDiscoveryLoadError` over the PREVIOUS results, which stay, and
once settled the RESULTS render the rails or the counted grid. TanStack Query is the source of truth for the results.

A retry from the results' refresh notice that succeeds moves focus to the frame's heading, across the boundary, as a
`useRecoverySignal` counter. Save a copy is `useSaveCopy`: each card derives its control from the clone mutation, and
the snackbar's Edit opens the copy.

implementations.name: DiscoverySortMenu
implementations.moduleDoc:
@commise/features-recipes/discovery — the web sort control of Discover: a ghost `sm` button "Sort: {choice}"
that opens a menu of four radio items with a check on the one in use (`docs/design/uiOverhaul/buildSpec.md` §4.5).
It is shown only while a query or filter is active, or after "See all".

An Adapter over Radix DropdownMenu, which carries the APG Menu Button model (arrow keys, Escape, focus return) and the
`menuitemradio` semantics; the trigger takes the design-system button's own surface class. It is the Discover twin of
`LibrarySortMenu`: the same shape over a different set of options, which a third menu would be the moment to share.

Presentational: it reports the chosen sort and holds only whether the menu is open.

implementations.name: RailLinkBox
implementations.moduleDoc:
@commise/features-recipes — the box a rail heading's "See all" link sits in (native).

The link wraps under its title when the two do not fit; it never shrinks or truncates, its target is at least 48 tall, and
its box is pulled back by the ghost button's padding so its TEXT sits on the title's start edge (designer ruling,
designAnswers.md 2026-11-01, "See all under its title"). The numbers are `railHeading.ts`'s, and `__tests__/RecipeBrowseRails.native.test.tsx` measures the rendered box.
Styled with Tamagui, so the screen file that holds the React Native styling ratchet adds nothing to it.

overlapping elements (e.g. multiple overlapping `View`s, or text and a
background).

expensive and hard to debug for non-native developers, which is why it is
not turned on by default.

implementations.name: RailTrack
implementations.moduleDoc:
@commise/features-recipes — web browse-rail TRACK: the one horizontal scroll container a rail's cards sit
in, whether they are loaded cards or loading placeholders (`docs/design/uiOverhaul/buildSpec.md` §4.4).

Both rail bodies render through this element so the pending strip and the loaded strip cannot drift apart. They
did once (E1, `docs/design/uiOverhaul/evaluateShellAndLists.md`): the skeleton strip had no overflow rule, so its
tiles widened the whole page at 320 px while only the loaded strip scrolled inside itself. The overflow belongs to
the track, and every tile inside it is a `shrink-0` item.

The loaded track is the design-system `HorizontalScroller`: a focusable `region` named "{rail} recipes", whose arrow keys
scroll it by one card, and each card is a tab stop of its own (SC 2.1.1). It snaps card by card, the next card peeks at
the edge — the swipe cue on touch — and a chevron hints at the cards beyond while it rests at its start. Its element and
its position are handed to the rail through `RailContext`, so the rail's Previous and Next move it and read the same
facts. A placeholder track is `aria-hidden` and does not scroll: its tiles carry no content, its rail's live region
speaks for it, and it has nothing to promise.

Presentational: the scrolling track of one rail; the scroll position is read from the host's context.

implementations.name: RecipeBrowseRails
implementations.moduleDoc:
@commise/features-recipes — web curated browse-rails block (presentational, U7; slice 5 of the UI overhaul).

The default discovery surface when nothing is searched: three fixed-sort rails (Trending/New/Quick), each an H2 with
"See all" over the rail's BODY, then "Browse by cuisine" as a scrolling row of chips, plus ONE notice for a failed
refresh of the block (`docs/design/uiOverhaul/buildSpec.md` §4.4). Each body is what that rail's own read boundary
renders (`RecipeBrowseRailLoading`, `RecipeBrowseRailLoadError` or `RecipeBrowseRailResults`), so a rail loads and fails
on its own while every heading stays put. It fetches nothing.

A fine pointer also gets Previous and Next (36 px round ghost buttons before "See all"); they move the rail's track one
view less one card and disable at the ends. The track is inside the body's boundary and the buttons outside it, so the
rail hands its body a `RailContext` and the track gives the rail its element back.

@commise/features-recipes — web discovery FRAME (presentational, T076 / US2; slice 5 of the UI overhaul).

The chrome of public discovery, rendered OUTSIDE the discovery suspense boundary, which the composing container passes as
`children`: the large title, the search field with its recent-search panel, the filters, back-to-browse, the sort, and
the count line (`docs/design/uiOverhaul/buildSpec.md` §3.3, §4.4, §4.5). A pending or failed search therefore swaps only
the results, never the field a viewer is typing in. It fetches nothing.

The filters arrive in the ONE presentation the container decided: a sticky panel beside the results (the search field,
count and results then share the column to its right), or a Filters button with the sort, the applied-filter chips and
the sheet — so the facets exist exactly once.

The two presentations are ONE tree: the search field, the count line and `children` keep their parent and index in
both, and only the slots around them fill or empty. The presentation follows `<main>`'s measured width, so it switches
right after the first paint on a wide screen and on every resize across the breakpoint. Drawn as two trees, each switch
remounted the field (focus and the recent-search panel gone), the live region (remounted with its text inside) and the
whole results body (every rail back at its start). The sort moves between the Filters row and the count line, so it
alone remounts; a sort menu held open through a resize closes. `RecipeDiscoveryContainer.layoutSwitch.test.tsx` and
this frame's "switching between the sheet and the panel" tests hold it.

The count line is one element that is both the visible "12 recipes for “lamb”" and the polite live region that announces
it. It is mounted empty with the frame and outlives every body the boundary swaps in (loading, error, no-result,
results), because a live region that mounts with its text already inside is not reliably announced. Identical results
stay silent; nothing is announced when a search starts. On a successful server prefetch it ships its text in the HTML,
which is correct: a page load should not announce its own results, and the first change after that does.

The one piece of local state is `searchFocused` — pure UI — because the recent-search panel (U7) is an IDLE-state
affordance: it appears only while focus is inside the search area and nothing is searched. The history behind it
belongs to the container's `useRecentSearches`. The heading takes focus when `headingFocusSignal` advances: a retry from
the results' refresh notice (inside the boundary) that succeeds removes the button the viewer pressed, and the container
reports that across the boundary.

implementations.name: RecipeDiscoveryFrame
implementations.moduleDoc:
@commise/features-recipes — native discovery FRAME (presentational, T076 / US2; slice 5 of the UI overhaul).

The React Native twin of `RecipeDiscoveryFrame`: the same chrome, pinned above the discovery suspense boundary that
arrives as `children`, so a pending or failed search never unmounts the field a viewer is typing in
(`docs/design/uiOverhaul/buildSpec.md` §3.3, §4.4, §4.5). The filters arrive in the ONE presentation the container
decided — a 256 pt panel beside the results on a tablet held wide, otherwise a Filters button with the sort, the
applied-filter chips and the sheet — and the count line is one visible element that is also the polite live region,
mounted empty with the frame so it outlives every body the boundary swaps in. Colour is read from the theme at render (D15).

Back-to-browse lives HERE, rather than in the result grid's scrolling header, where it existed only while results
rendered: a "see all" whose list was still loading or had failed would have left no way back to the rails. It shows only
after a "see all", so it costs the pinned area one 44pt row only in the state that needs it.

Like its web twin it owns one piece of local UI state — `searchFocused` — gating the recent-search panel (U7) to the
idle state. The heading takes the screen-reader cursor when `headingFocusSignal` advances.

## Compact height (`docs/design/compactHeightLayout.md` §5.4)

Sideways, the stacked chrome left the results 16 to 76 dp, and about 0 with the keyboard open. In compact height
(`useCompactHeight`) the heading shares a wrapping row with the field, and the filter trigger, back to browse and the
sort share one wrapping row, in the same reading order. While compact AND a keyboard is open (`useFrameCollapsed`)
AND the frame's own field has focus, that controls row steps aside; a keyboard raised by the filter sheet's search
leaves it alone, because the row holds the trigger and the sheet it keeps open. ⛔ Two groups hold the chrome in EVERY
layout, the field the header group's last child, so the field never changes parent or index: a remounted field would
lose focus and its keyboard. The recent-search rows scroll in every layout, and the first tap with the keyboard up lands
on a query. A compact window is never wide enough for the panel (`filterPresentationOf`), so the sheet presentation is
the only one it sees. *
## Switching between the sheet and the panel

The same rule holds across the panel: both presentations are ONE tree, so turning a tablet across the breakpoint keeps
the field (focused, keyboard up), the count line and the whole results body mounted. Only the title moves, above the
panel row. `RecipeDiscoveryFrame.native.test.tsx` ("switching between the sheet and the panel") holds it.

implementations.name: RecipeDiscoveryLoadError
implementations.moduleDoc:
@commise/features-recipes — web discovery LOAD ERROR body (presentational; slice 5 of the UI overhaul).

What the discovery suspense boundary renders when a search failed (`docs/design/uiOverhaul/buildSpec.md` §4.6): "We
couldn't search right now." and a Try again under the field, for any cause — offline included, because a screen never
changes behaviour for being offline. The results that were on screen before the failure stay under the message
(`previous`); a first load that fails has none. The message is an `alert`, so a retry that fails again is announced; the
previous results sit OUTSIDE it so they are not read as part of the alert.

implementations.name: RecipeDiscoveryResults
implementations.moduleDoc:
@commise/features-recipes — web discovery RESULTS (presentational, T076 / US2; slice 5 of the UI overhaul).

What the discovery suspense boundary renders once a search has settled, below the frame: the curated rails while
browsing; a no-result state — a search, filters, or both — that always ends in tag chips and the Trending rail, so the
page is never a dead end; or the cards in the variant the host decided (compact 2-up below a 600 container, grid from
600) with their Save a copy footers and an explicit load-more control, plus the notice for a failed refresh
(`docs/design/uiOverhaul/buildSpec.md` §4.5, §4.6). It fetches nothing. The count line is the frame's: one element that
is both the visible line and the polite live region.

While newer results are pending (`stale`), these stay at full strength and fully usable: dimming would take the card
text under 4.5:1, and they can still be opened or copied. The design-system `PendingBar` appears above them after a
delay. ⛔ The region is deliberately NOT `aria-busy`: JAWS hides content marked busy, which would take away the very
results this state keeps usable.

implementations.name: RecipeDiscoveryResults
implementations.moduleDoc:
@commise/features-recipes — native discovery RESULTS (presentational, T076 / US2; slice 5 of the UI overhaul).

The React Native twin of `RecipeDiscoveryResults`: the rails while browsing; a no-result state — a search, filters, or
both — that always ends in tag chips and the Trending rail, so the page is never a dead end; or the cards in the
variant the host decided (compact 2-up below a 600 container, grid from 600) in a virtualised list with the load-more
footer, plus the notice for a failed refresh (`docs/design/uiOverhaul/buildSpec.md` §4.5, §4.6). It fetches nothing.
The count line is the frame's.

The results are a `FlashList`, which both scrolls and recycles cells, with pull-to-refresh bound to the result list.
The rails bring their own scroll container and their own pull (`RecipeBrowseRails`), so while browsing this leaf
renders the slot as it is — a pull there refreshes the rails on screen, never the results hidden behind them.

While newer results are pending (`stale`) the results stay readable and usable and the design-system `PendingBar`
appears after its delay. ⛔ Not `aria-busy`: a screen reader may hide busy content, and these results must stay
readable. The bar sits on this container, OUTSIDE the list, so it does not scroll away with the header. Colour is read
from the theme at render (D15).

implementations.name: EditorActionBar
implementations.moduleDoc:
@commise/features-recipes/editor — the web editor's action bar (build spec §7.1, §7.8): Preview, then the
primary at the end — Publish for a recipe not yet published, Save changes for a published one. Sticky at the foot of
the form column at every width; the one glass surface of the editor (owner D12), readable with the blur off. When the
header and the bar together are taller than half the viewport (`compactHeightLayout.md` A1) it is not sticky: it
scrolls with the page as the column's last content, in the same place in the page, so a focused control keeps focus.

After a refused Publish, a polite line says how many things to fix (SC 3.3.1). While lines have no match, a quiet
polite line says the recipe is ready and that those lines' nutrition is left out (owner D20); Publish stays enabled. A finishing write shows the primary
busy and locks the bar.

Presentational: props → JSX. Its node leaves through `placeRef`, so the page can measure it.

@commise/features-recipes/editor — one editor section (build spec §7.1, §7.10): a region named by its H2, the
heading row with the section's own controls at its end, then the body.

The H2's id is the section's id (`sections.ts`), which is what the section index links to, the hash names and the
page's `ScrollHost` jumps to; it carries `tabIndex={-1}` so a jump can move focus to it. A jump lands it 16 px under
the sticky chrome (build spec §7.2): the document's `scroll-padding-top` is the chrome (`useEditorScrollPadding`,
§7.10) and `scrollIntoView` adds this heading's `scroll-margin-top` to it, so the margin is the 16 px alone.

It tells the leaves inside whether it is the section the cook is in (`sectionPresence.ts`).

Presentational: props → JSX.

implementations.name: IngredientStatusPoller
implementations.moduleDoc:
Headless poll-after-add for one food-backed ingredient line (data-model R5 / FR-007), for both apps. When the picker
adds a line that came back `PENDING` (nutrition still resolving), the editor renders ONE of these per pending line:
it drives `useIngredientStatus` (which self-limits — it refetches only while the food is `PENDING` and stops the
instant a terminal/`RESOLVED`/`UNRESOLVED` state arrives) and reports every observed status back up via `onStatus`,
so the editor can flip the line's badge from `PENDING` to `RESOLVED` (or surface `UNRESOLVED` for disambiguation, or
a terminal state).

It renders nothing — the visible status lives on the form's own per-line badge. The editor makes `onStatus`
idempotent (`settleIngredientLine` no-ops an unchanged answer) so the repeated callback cannot loop, and unmounts this
poller once the line leaves `PENDING` (which also stops the query).
implementations.description: Poll one pending food-backed line to resolution.

tags.name: param
tags.text: props - The line's ingredient id + the status-report callback.

tags.name: returns
tags.text: Nothing (headless) — the line's badge is rendered by the form.

props.name: ingredientId
props.description: The binding of the pending line to poll.

props.name: onStatus
props.description:
Called with the polled id and what the poll observed — the binding the server answered with (a different id once
the line settled, plan 002) and its status. Must be idempotent.

cannot keep it - every private slot is used, or the recipe is an imported public-web one that needs Premium and a change
of the cook's own (owner ruling 2026-10-26). A polite dialog with two choices of EQUAL weight, side by side, neither
preselected: Keep as draft and Publish as public.

implementations.moduleDoc:
@commise/features-recipes/editor — `PublishOpenChoicesSheet` (web): what the editor asks before publishing a
recipe whose lines have no food yet (`docs/design/uiRefreshWorkshop5/redesignCanvas/ingredientMatching.md`, R23).
Publishing stays allowed. The sheet says the open lines are saved as written and do not count toward nutrition, names
a line still being checked, and says how many lines count; Choose now and Publish anyway are the two ways on.

On the design-system `Sheet`, not `ConfirmDialog`: that primitive is for a destructive step, and publishing is not one.
At narrow the two actions stack, Publish anyway LAST, nearest the thumb; from the `nav` width they share a row, the
primary at its end. The DOM order is the visual order at every width, so Tab and the eye agree (U11).

Choose now hands off AFTER the sheet is gone (`onDismissed`), not on the press: the host opens the first open line and asks
it for focus, and the sheet's own close then returns focus to its opener (Publish). Handing off on the press lost that
race and left the cook on Publish. The state is only the intent to hand off, so the component still renders props.

Presentational: props in, markup out; the words are `openChoicesCopyOf`'s. The native leaf is
`./PublishOpenChoicesSheet.native.tsx`.

implementations.name: RecipeEditorSurface
implementations.moduleDoc:
What both apps' editor screens draw over a {@link RecipeEditorSession}: the section map (each section's real leaves),
the Ingredients status pollers, the heading actions (Paste a list, Paste steps), the rail foot, and the preview, upsell
and make-public sheets. The web `RecipeEditorContainer` and the native `RecipeEditorScreen` each carried this JSX
line for line (UI audit 10); every leaf it uses is already a web/native pair, so this one file serves both.

What stays in the app, and why:
- how the editor is SEEDED and where its URL or route goes: the web reads `?draft=`, `?fresh=` and `#section`, and
  redirects a recipe the server holds; a phone has no URL, so a new recipe's draft is found again only within the
  session that made it (ADR-0057, blueprint A4). That is a platform difference, not drift;
- the photo uploader ({@link RecipeEditorSurfaceProps.renderPhotos}), which each app wires to its own picker;
- the navigation port, the profile read and the error reporter, which are the session's inputs.

⚠️ The uploader is asked for only once the recipe exists on the server (its first checkpoint, which needs a title):
the upload takes a recipe id, and a picked photo's bytes cannot live in the device draft (ADR-0057).

implementations.name: RecipeEditorView
implementations.moduleDoc:
@commise/features-recipes/editor — the web one-page recipe editor (build spec §7; owner decisions D1, D2, D3,
D12): the header, the section index, the four sections, the action bar and the notices, over the editor's lifecycle
(`useRecipeEditor`). Create and edit are this one page.

ORCHESTRATION of the page: it owns the page's one `ScrollHost`, and draws what `useEditorPage` decides (the statuses
from the one validator, the chrome, the checkpoints, the announcements, the commands). The web adds only what the
browser alone has: work the server does not hold yet arms the browser's own unload prompt (D7), the
popups keep clear of the sticky chrome (the header and the index box stuck under it), and when the header and the
action bar together are taller than half the viewport (`compactHeightLayout.md` A1) the bar scrolls with the page and
the section bar hides (build spec §7.1). The sections' bodies are the container's, which owns their data.

No back-to-top control (D3). The editor's glass is its action bar only (D12). × never asks (Settled 24).

implementations.moduleDoc:
@commise/features-recipes/filters — the web filter groups (`docs/design/uiOverhaul/buildSpec.md` §4.4): the
ONE facet tree that the Discover panel and the filter sheet both draw. The container renders exactly one of them, so
there is one set of names for assistive technology to find.

Each group is a named `group` (or, for a time ladder, a `radiogroup`) with its name as a small heading above it. The name
lives once in the accessibility tree — on the row — and the visible name is hidden from it, so a screen reader
does not say "Dietary, Dietary". Total time is a choice with an "Any"; prep and cook time sit behind one native
disclosure; a chip group shows twelve chips then "Show all ({n})", and a chosen chip is never behind it; the
ingredient typeahead is a search field with its results and its chosen ingredients as removable chips.

Its state is UI state only: which groups were opened to show all, and focus intent (SC 2.4.3). The result or chip the
cook pressed unmounts on every ingredient add and removal, so focus moves to whatever then holds the search slot once
the press lands (`useIngredientPressLanding`); a filter a URL fills moves nothing.

Presentational: it draws the facet groups from the view and reports every change.

A presentational leaf: it renders `useAuthoredFoodCreate`'s state, which the field group passes in, and reports every

  (WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.3), so busy and refused controls go through `busyControlProps` and `refusedPressProps`.

the pure `addChip` (trimmed, a duplicate in any case dropped). A comma is read in the text itself, so a pasted
"a, b, c" adds `a` and `b` and keeps `c` being typed. Leaving the field adds what was typed, so nothing typed is
lost silently. The native leaf (`ChipInput.native.tsx`) shares this contract.

@commise/features-recipes/form — `PasteChoicePane` (web): the side pane at 1194 and on web
(`docs/design/uiRefreshWorkshop5/redesignCanvas/ingredientMatching.md`). A named `aside`: which line it shows out of
ALL the recipe's lines ("Line 3 of 9", M4), the line as its heading, the muted prompt, a pick that did not save with
Try again, the line's `FoodChoiceList`, then Previous and Next open line (`paneStepsOf`).

Previous and Next are always drawn and are refused at an end — focusable, the press cancelled, never natively
disabled, because the step that reaches the end is the one holding focus (WCAG 2.4.3) — so nothing moves under the
cook and the pair never changes shape (a top-level `hasNext && <Button>` would also be §11.2's boolean-selects-a-subtree). A pick in the pane
does not move on by itself (staff-ux ruling 2026-10-25): the check appears on the row, and Next moves on.

Presentational: props in, markup out. The native leaf is `./PasteChoicePane.native.tsx`.

implementations.moduleDoc:
@commise/features-recipes/form — `RecipeBasicsFields` (web): the one-page editor's Details section
(`docs/design/uiOverhaul/buildSpec.md` §7.4), in four H3 groups. The editor frame renders the section's H2.

- About the recipe: the title (one line however it arrives, a soft 120 limit counted on the trimmed text) and the
  description (a soft cap with a counter from 80%).
- Time and servings: a stepper, prep and cook as durations that never show a "0", and the computed total.
- Kind of dish: the cuisine (free text with the suggested list, `useCuisineField`), and the meal-type and difficulty
  choice rows, each clearable.
- Diet and tags: the two chip inputs.

Presentational and controlled: every edit goes up through `onChange`. The one listener on the frame reports a field
leaving focus (`onFieldBlur`, the editor's checkpoint) and keeps Enter out of the title; both events bubble, so the
design-system fields need no props for them. The native leaf is `./RecipeBasicsFields.native.tsx`.

props, the same pure rules (`./fieldText.ts`, `./minutesDuration.ts`) and the same copy.

What differs from web, and why:
- The layout follows the container class of the window's width (`useContainerClass`): below 600 prep and cook share
  a row and servings sits above them; from 600 servings, prep and cook share one row, and cuisine sits beside meal
  type. Web reads the same thresholds through `@regular/main:` variants.
- The title's return key is not blocked, because React Native has no cancellable key event; `singleLine` turns the
  break into a space instead, as it does a pasted one on both platforms.
- `onFieldBlur` is not called: no design-system field reports its blur on native, and React Native does not bubble
  focus events. The editor's other checkpoints still save the draft.
- Colours come from the theme at render, so both colour schemes paint (owner D15).

implementations.name: RecipeVisibilityField
implementations.moduleDoc:
@commise/features-recipes/form — `RecipeVisibilityField` (web): "Who can see it"
(`docs/design/uiOverhaul/buildSpec.md` §7.7 item 2), a radio group of two cards, Public and Private.

Every recipe offers Private (ADR-0073). Private
works within the cook's private slots (ADR-0073): the card says how many are left, and with none left it is refused
with three ways forward (`slotsFull`). Under the premium rule's `upsell` (an imported public-web recipe), Private carries
the Premium badge and choosing it calls `onPremiumRequired` instead of changing the value: the upsell decides, and
nothing is pre-selected for it (`visibilityChoice`). A recipe that is already private stays private and shows so.
Choosing Public on it calls `onConfirmPublic` where that costs something worth saying (it frees a slot) — the confirm
decides — and the Public card says beforehand what it costs (`visibilityFieldOf`; plan 2026-10-14-009 D14, Q5).

Presentational and controlled. The native leaf is `./RecipeVisibilityField.native.tsx`.

@commise/features-recipes/format — a text that shows recipe amounts, on the web (UI Designer ruling Q5).

@commise/features-recipes/import — `ImportFlaggedList` (web): "N to check" (board FlaggedLine), the lines the
save-time check doubts after a "Pick the best match for me" import. Each row names its line and recipe and the doubted
match, then ONE action — "Use Whole milk", when the check has a food to offer — and "Choose another", named "Choose
another food for {line}", with a 44 px target. Choose another opens the line's options, search first: the sheet below

words, with Try again, and the page has ONE polite live region (M6, U9).

implementations.name: ImportWizardNotice
implementations.moduleDoc:
@commise/features-recipes/import — `ImportWizardNotice`: what the review says in place of a step it cannot
show (board WizardStates). Loading names the recipe being read; an error names the recipe, says the choices so far are
saved, and offers Try again and Skip this recipe; offline says the choices are kept on the device and the review
resumes by itself — with no control, because there is nothing the cook must do (the `OfflineReadSlot` contract).

The board's two other states are not here, on purpose: a recipe with nothing to fix is a step whose lines are all
matched (`ImportLineList` says so), and a review with no recipe to review has no step at all — every recipe is added
without one and the import ends at `ImportSummary`.

ONE component for both platforms: it composes only the design system's notices, which resolve to their web or native
leaf at bundle time.

Presentational: props → JSX; the host decides what Try again and Skip do.

implementations.name: FoodChoiceList
implementations.moduleDoc:
@commise/features-recipes/ingredientMatching — `FoodChoiceList` (web): the ONE list a line's food is chosen
from, in both flows (`docs/design/uiRefreshWorkshop5/redesignCanvas/ingredientMatching.md`, owner rulings
2026-10-25). Search for a food first (ruling I1), at its own width so its words start at the rows' edge (U5); then ONE
bordered box on the raised paper (U2) holding the options in the server's order, the default with its quiet Default
tag (`OptionLabel`), and "Keep “line” as written · no nutrition" as its last row in the quiet ink (U6), rules between
the rows. Offline, the words "Search needs the network" stand where search was.

- ⛔ Each option is a BUTTON (`ChoiceRow`), and pressing it is the pick (staff-ux ruling 2026-10-25). A radio group
  would check the option the arrow keys land on, so moving through the list would pick a food and carry the cook to
  the next line (WCAG 3.2.2), and could pick the default, which the owner ruled is never chosen for the cook.
- Nothing is drawn chosen until the cook has chosen: the bound food of a reopened line draws a check and its name ends
  ", chosen", so the state never rests on colour (1.4.1). No `aria-current` as well: it would say the state twice.
- While a send is in flight the control that started it spins and reads busy — the row, or Search for a food found
  through it — and every other control is refused: focusable, the press cancelled, dimmed (2.4.3). None is ever
  natively disabled, because any of them may hold focus when the send starts.
- A focus request lands on the view's `focusTarget`: Search, else the first option, else Keep, so it is always taken.
- When Try again unmounts because a retry started, focus lands on the view's `landing`: the control that send made busy
  (still drawn, refused, never natively disabled), so focus is never dropped to the page (2.4.3).
- Rows are 48 px at least, in the 14 px `list` role; long names wrap and never truncate, so nothing scrolls sideways
  at 320 px.

Presentational: props in, markup out; what it shows is `matchLineView.ts`'s. The native leaf is
`./FoodChoiceList.native.tsx`.

implementations.name: FoodChoiceList
implementations.moduleDoc:
@commise/features-recipes/ingredientMatching — `FoodChoiceList` (native): the React Native leaf of
`./FoodChoiceList.tsx`, on the same props and the same words (`matchLineView.ts`). Search for a food first, at its own
width (U5); then ONE bordered box on the raised paper (U2) holding the options in the server's order, the default
tagged (`OptionLabel`), and "Keep “line” as written · no nutrition" as its last row in the quiet ink (U6), hairlines
between the rows.

Each option is a `ChoiceRow`, a `button` (staff-ux ruling 2026-10-25): VoiceOver and TalkBack read a radio as "not
selected", which implies a confirm step that does not exist. The bound food draws a check and its name ends
", chosen"; no `selected` state as well, which would say it twice. While a send is in flight the control that started
it spins and reads busy, and every other control is disabled and dimmed (a disabled `Pressable` keeps screen-reader
focus on device). The box is a `list` named for its line, its rows `listitem`s, so the name is announced with the
count and marks where this line's list starts (U12; `docs/design/nativeContainerNames.md` N1 rules 4 and 5); the list
keeps its native node for that role. A focus request moves the screen-reader cursor to the view's `focusTarget`; a retry that
starts moves it to the view's `landing`, the control that send made busy.
Rows keep the native touch floor and every name wraps, so nothing is cut off or scrolls sideways at 320 pt. Painted
from the theme's roles (D15).

@commise/features-recipes/ingredientMatching — `MatchSettledRow` (web): a matched line that needs nothing from
the cook now, in either flow (`docs/design/uiRefreshWorkshop5/redesignCanvas/ingredientMatching.md`). The line as the
cook wrote it, then its status — a bound food said whole with a check (and the Default tag on a default nobody but the
server chose), a proposal under review with its tag, or a sentence — then, on their own line, the controls its state
allows, and a late review result's one quiet sentence with See why.

- Each control is named for its line, because the same control shows on many lines (2.4.6, 2.5.3).

  busy and the others refuse a press, so a double tap cannot send two. A refused control stays focusable (`refused`,
  never native `disabled`): it may hold focus when the send starts (M2, 2.4.3).
- A send that did not save says so, with Try again (`MatchFailureLine`, M6).
- The line is 16 px; its status, actions' words and note are the 14 px `list` role (owner type-scale ruling). A rule
  sits above it, as above every line (U3).

says so, with Try again (M6). The status and the note are the 14 pt `list` role; `MatchLineList` draws the rule above
the line. Painted from the theme's roles, so it reads in both themes (D15).

implementations.name: SeeWhy
implementations.moduleDoc:
@commise/features-recipes/ingredientMatching — `SeeWhy` (web): the VISIBLE disclosure behind "See why"
(owner design 2026-10-26, "INTERACTION GAPS"). It used to be spoken only — the reason went to the list's polite region
and nowhere else — so a cook who looked away, or cannot hear it, never saw why. The link now toggles `aria-expanded`,
the reason opens in place under the row in the 14 px muted `meta` role, it is announced once (on opening, through
`onOpen`), and pressing again closes it.

It holds the one bit of state a disclosure has — open or closed — because nothing else reads it: the host owns the
announcement, not the visibility. A row that remounts closes it, which is the right reading of "tap again closes".
The native leaf is `./SeeWhy.native.tsx`.

Orchestration: it holds the open state, so it is not a pure render leaf.

implementations.moduleDoc:
@commise/features-recipes — the few boxes the Recipes list is laid out with (native).

The list is full width so its header can scroll with it, which makes the 16 pt side gutter the list's own job: the
header insets itself, and each row, the empty body, the footer and the chips/result bar carry it through {@link ListEdge}.
Styled with Tamagui tokens, so the screen files that hold the React Native styling ratchet add nothing to it. The pinned search
field's own parts are `@commise/ui/pinned-search`'s.

This is a special performance property exposed by `RCTView` and is useful
for scrolling content when there are many subviews, most of which are
offscreen. For this property to be effective, it must be applied to a
view that contains many subviews that extend outside its bound. The
subviews must also have `overflow: hidden`, as should the containing view
(or one of its superviews).

See https://reactnative.dev/docs/view#removeclippedsubviews

props.name: renderToHardwareTextureAndroid
props.description:
Whether this `View` should render itself (and all of its children) into a
single hardware texture on the GPU.

On Android, this is useful for animations and interactions that only
modify opacity, rotation, translation and/or scale: in those cases, the
view does not have to be redrawn and display lists do not need to be
re-executed. The texture can be re-used and re-composited with different
parameters. The downside is that this can use up limited video memory, so
this prop should be set back to `false` at the end of the interaction/
animation.
@platform android

shouldRasterizeIOS
props.description:
Whether this `View` should be rendered as a bitmap before compositing.

On iOS, this is useful for animations and interactions that do not
modify this component's dimensions nor its children; for example, when
translating the position of a static view, rasterization allows the
renderer to skip re-rendering the view frame and re-use the cached
bitmap.

Rasterization incurs an offscreen drawing pass and the bitmap consumes
memory. Test and measure when using this property.

components.name: HostAnimatedScroll
patterns: Adapter — a host-fed Animated scroll view behind FlashList's `renderScrollComponent` seam

implementations.name: HostAnimatedScroll
implementations.moduleDoc:
@commise/features-recipes — the scroll view the Recipes list renders (native), with the host's scroll offset
attached to it natively.

FlashList renders its scroller through `Animated.createAnimatedComponent` and lets a screen supply it with
`renderScrollComponent`. This is that scroller: an `Animated.ScrollView` whose `onScroll` is an `Animated.event` on the
`ScrollHost`'s `scrollY` (`useNativeDriver`), with FlashList's OWN handler as the listener, so recycling and viewability
run as before and FlashList still calls the host's plain `bind.onScroll`. The offset drives the pinned search field on the
native thread, with no JS per frame beyond the handlers that already ran.

It replaces `AnimatedFlashList`: wrapping FlashList itself in `Animated.createAnimatedComponent` threw "Maximum update
depth exceeded" on iOS and Android (the stack started `at FlashList ... at Animated(Anonymous)`).

A render function FlashList calls inside its own scroller component, so hooks are legal here; FlashList memoises the
scroller on this function's IDENTITY, so it must stay a module-level constant, never an inline function.

moduleTags.name: module
moduleTags.text: @commise/features-recipes — the scroll view the Recipes list renders (native), with the host's scroll offset

moduleTags.name: pattern
moduleTags.text: Adapter — a host-fed Animated scroll view behind FlashList's `renderScrollComponent` seam

implementations.description:
Orchestration: reads the host's scroll offset and builds the one native-driven `Animated.event` over it (a hook and an Animated
node), then hands the Animated scroll view its props. It holds no ref.

tags.text: props - What FlashList hands its scroller: its `onScroll` handler, its ref and the host's other scroll props.

tags.name: returns

components.name: ListEdge

implementations.name: ListEdge
implementations.moduleDoc:
@commise/features-recipes — the few boxes the Recipes list is laid out with (native).

The list is full width so its header can scroll with it, which makes the 16 pt side gutter the list's own job: the
header insets itself, and each row, the empty body, the footer and the chips/result bar carry it through {@link ListEdge}.
Styled with Tamagui tokens, so the screen files that hold the React Native styling ratchet add nothing to it. The pinned search
field's own parts are `@commise/ui/pinned-search`'s.
